title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rotary/rope optimizations
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: This PR upgrades the attention execution path to use FlashAttentionV2 kernels where available and introduces a set of fused operators and rotary/rope optimizations to reduce memory traffic and kernel-launch overhead. Motivation: production inference latency and token throughput remain the primary cost drivers for our Dedicated and Private customers (ENG-4271). FlashAttentionV2 enables lower memory bandwidth for causal attention; fused ops reduce intermediate writes for common attention patterns; and rope/rotary changes reduce per-token compute for long-context workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce runtime/attention/flash_attention_v2.cu - new kernel selection and compatibility shim for existing attention ops. 2) Add fused_ops.cu - fused QKV + attention + projection for common transformer blocks to eliminate redundant GEMM->transpose steps. 3) Optimize rotary/rope math path to apply exponentiated rotations in-register for supported data types. 4) Hooked kernel selection into scheduler to prefer low-latency variants under 95th-percentile SLOs and fallback to existing kernels on unsupported GPUs. 5) KV cache manager heuristics updated to keep prefix KV in pinned GPU memory and enable fast path when using fused ops. 6) Continuous batcher updated to detect FlashAttentionV2-friendly request shapes and form micro-batches that maximize warp utilization. Commits (high level): - fc1f3b2: add FlashAttentionV2 kernels and build/test harness - 9a4d0c1: fused ops implementation + API glue - 7b2a6d4: rotary/rope micro-optimizations and unit tests - d3c5e1a: scheduler heuristics + fallback routes - b8f7c22: bench updates and docs Benchmarks: micro-bench on an A100 (seq_len=1024, bs=8) shows: - baseline (flashv1/fallback): 18.3 ms per token - FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops: 11.9 ms per token (~35% latency reduction) - throughput improved from 450 tokens/s to 720 tokens/s for this shape. Long-context (seq_len=4096) memory footprint reduced by ~28% with rope optimizations. Compatibility: automatic fallback to legacy kernels on older CUDA/SM versions; runtime will log a one-time WARN the first time a kernel variant is unavailable. Tests & CI: added unit tests for fused ops and rotary math; updated GPU integration tests in ci/pipeline/interop_gpu_tests.yaml. CI: GPU integration matrix passed; perf benchmarks run in nightly bench job. Review conversation (summary): - Liam: requested clearer docs on when FlashAttentionV2 is selected and a knob to force legacy for debugging. Addressed: added selection logs and REDWOOD_FORCE_LEGACY_ATTENTION env var. - Diego: asked for correctness tests across dtypes (fp16/ bf16/ int8); we added coverage for fp16 and bf16, left int8 as experimental behind a flag. - Anya: questioned KV cache pinning safety for multi-tenant Dedicated pools; we added a conservative heuristic and feature flag (kv_cache_pin_threshold) to enable per-customer opt-in. - Marcus: asked to validate performance on multicard pipeline; results added to benchmarks. Merge & rollout: merged using squash; rollout plan: gradual canary across Dedicated pools with a canary percentage and automatic rollback on latency/regression alerts. Release notes: "Attention runtime: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rotary optimizations — up to ~35% latency reduction and memory savings for long-context workloads. Automatic fallback enabled for unsupported hardware."
